This is done to ensure that two calls with the same arguments but different redacted values are not mistaken for repeats. {"question": "How is a tool call's args_hash computed?"}

The `args_hash` is computed as `sha256(tool_name ∖0 canonical_json(args))[:16]`, which is a 16-character hash of the tool name and the canonical JSON representation of the arguments. This is done to ensure that two calls with the same arguments but different redacted values are not mistaken for repeats. If a low-entropy argument hash is a concern, an HMAC key can be used to make the hash irreversible. [docs/TRACE_SCHEMA.md]
